newsitem.title: USA: Prudential raises Intel price target.
newsitem.headline: Prudential raises Intel price target.

text.p: Prudential Securities analyst Mark Edelstone said Thursday he had raised his 12-month price target on Intel Corp to $170 from $150.
He also confirmed he had raised his 1996 and 1997 earnings estimates on the leading chip maker.

Edelstone cited several reasons for his moves, including a belief that Intel continues to attract buyers to its highest priced chips and has not had to cut prices on its Pentium chip. "It's also at a time when capacity utilization is very high. Therefore, gross margins are extremely high," he said.
As for the recent voracious buying of Intel's stock, which surged 7-3/4 Wednesday in a broadly lower market, he said, "There's no expectation of a repeat (rise in the stock) in 1997."
He maintains his buy rating on Intel.
Edelstone raised his per-share earnings estimates on Intel to $5.70 from $5.50 for 1996, and to $8.85 from $7.40 for 1997.
He said the stock has jumped "as we come to year-end and portfolio managers are trying to maximize performance."
"It has been a difficult market for the average fund and they're looking for highly liquid names that are not excessively valued," he said.
He does not believe Intel is excessively valued.
Edelstone still favors three other companies in his group -- Advanced Micro Devices Inc, up 7/8 to 27-3/4; LSI Logic Corp, up 1/4 to 31-1/8; and National Semiconductor Corp, up 7/8 to 27-3/8.
He said these companies "have the potential for positive earnings surprises" next year."
Asked about Cypress Semiconductor Corp, which has posted gains in very active trading recently, Edelstone said he has a hold rating on the stock.
"The stock is well off its highs and people are looking for stocks that lagged. You can argue that the company's results are now bottoming," he said.

As for the overall group, he said, "It has had a tremendous move since the industry turned in July, and at this point you have to pay attention to valuation. The risk going forward is the stocks will be ahead of the fundamentals."
